paragraphs.en: The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after groundbreaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children's literacy and emotional development. But only if you act him out.
paragraphs.zh: 那位出身于埃文河畔斯特拉特福文法学校的男孩，在学术界有力地证明了自己的价值：一项突破性研究表明，莎士比亚的作品确实有益于儿童读写能力和情感的发展。不过，前提是要把他的作品演出来。

paragraphs.en: A study found that a "rehearsal room" approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened children's vocabulary and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy. "The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves," Jacqui O'Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said.
paragraphs.zh: 一项研究发现，以“排练室”的方式教授莎士比亚作品，不仅拓宽了儿童的词汇量，提高了他们写作的复杂程度，也提升了他们的情感素养。委托开展这项研究的皇家莎士比亚剧团（RSC）的雅基·奥汉隆说：“研究表明，演员的工作方式会极大地影响儿童运用语言的方式，以及他们看待自己的方式。”

paragraphs.en: The randomised control trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils aged nine and ten—at 45 state primary schools that had not been "previously exposed to RSC pedagogy". They were split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as Ferdinand after the shipwreck in *The Tempest*. The target group was given a 30-minute drama-based activity to accompany the passage.
paragraphs.zh: 这项随机对照试验涉及45所公立小学的数百名五年级学生，他们的年龄为九岁和十岁，此前都“没有接触过皇家莎士比亚剧团的教学方法”。学生被分为实验组和对照组，并被要求完成写作任务，例如，以《暴风雨》中遭遇海难后的费迪南德的身份，写一封漂流瓶里的信。实验组还参加了一项与所读段落配套、时长30分钟的戏剧活动。

paragraphs.en: The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words "classed as more sophisticated or rarer", and wrote at greater length. They also "appear to be more comfortable writing in role … while [control] pupils imagine how they themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character's emotion".
paragraphs.zh: 经过同行评审的研究结果表明，实验组学生运用了更丰富的词汇，使用了“被归为更复杂或更罕见的词语”，而且写出的篇幅更长。他们还“似乎更善于以角色的身份写作……对照组学生想象的是自己遭遇海难会如何反应，而实验组儿童则设身处地地站在文学角色的立场上，表达这个角色的情感”。

paragraphs.en: The Time to Act study also found that while control pupils relied on "desert island clichés" such as palm trees, target pupils were "more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions".
paragraphs.zh: 这项名为“行动时刻”的研究还发现，对照组学生依赖棕榈树之类的“荒岛描写老套意象”，而实验组学生的“描写范围更广，对天空、海洋和天气状况的呈现更为全面”。

paragraphs.en: O'Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the "emotional literacy that was evident in the [target] children's writing" and that they were "more resilient in their writing, more hopeful". She added: "The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through. They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes." The study showed the importance of embedding arts in education, she said.
paragraphs.zh: 奥汉隆说，最令她感到惊讶的是“实验组儿童的写作中明显体现出的情感素养”，而且他们“在写作中表现得更有韧性，更充满希望”。她补充说：“他们对情感的理解非常明显，这很可能与排练室的活动过程有关：在这个过程中，你会习惯于尝试通过想象来体验情境。他们能够自如地描述不同的情绪状态，而戏剧活动的一部分，就是设身处地地体验不同角色。”她说，这项研究表明了将艺术融入教育的重要性。

paragraphs.en: But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist? O'Hanlon said more research would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare's use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a "massive expansion of language into children's lives", which was combined with children "using their whole bodies to bring words to life".
paragraphs.zh: 不过，换成随便哪位剧作家的作品，也能重现这样的结果吗？奥汉隆说，这需要更多研究，但她认为，与日常使用的2,000个词相比，莎士比亚使用的20,000个词让“儿童生活中的语言得到了极大的拓展”，同时，孩子们还“运用整个身体让文字鲜活起来”。
